question: GQ-009
subject: a treadmill I built: every ingest would have blocked a push
what_happened_last_turn: the hook refused my push because 10 ledger entries disagreed. I re-derived grounding, refreshed the ledger, pushed clean — and treated it as a one-off.

it_was_not_a_one_off.what_trips_it: writing a want-list, which every ingest does
it_was_not_a_one_off.so: each future ingest = one blocked push + ten hand-refreshed entries, forever

the_measurement_that_settled_it.conclusion: the trigger blocked a push over a file that ZERO claims ground in

the_precedent_was_already_in_the_file: the comment above "schema change" says a trigger that fires on maintenance trains you to dismiss it — I had narrowed that one for exactly this reason on 2026-08-04 and left its neighbour broad

measured_over_full_history.meaning: 7 maintenance commits will no longer block a push; both genuine contract changes still caught

a_test_of_mine_that_was_wrong.what: built a scratch repo, touched the want-list, expected no trigger — got all three firing
a_test_of_mine_that_was_wrong.cause: the scratch copy has ONE synthetic base commit touching every watched path at once
a_test_of_mine_that_was_wrong.same_artefact: broke the gates-are-load-bearing baseline earlier today
a_test_of_mine_that_was_wrong.lesson: a git-history gate cannot be tested on synthetic history; test the pathspec against the real log
